# Ivan de Murard, Product Builder

## Identity

Homepage statement: "Product builder. Agentic AI systems for operations." Currently building an architecture of specialised agents for hotel operations.

Ivan de Murard is a product builder based in Paris, France. He has five years of product management experience across start-ups, scale-ups and large groups, plus two years as co-founder and product lead of Sonor, a B2G SaaS for urban noise mapping. He designs from operational experience, ships with AI, and keeps the human at the center.

Contact: ivandemurard@gmail.com. Booking: https://cal.com/ivandemurard/discussion-and-introduction. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ivandemurard/. GitHub: https://github.com/IvandeMurard.

## Convictions

1. Human interactions first. Technology should give time back to people, not pull them deeper into screens. The best automation is the one that lets a host be more present.
2. Real business value. Reducing operational costs, freeing capacity, sharpening decisions. Every product has to move a number that matters to the business.
3. Full-stack 0 to 1 craft. From insight to shipped product, bridging digital interfaces and physical operations, so the experience holds together end to end.

## How he works

1. Reading the ground. Field-level fluency in operations: boutique hotels, F&B, design partners, open-data ecosystems. He learns an environment before he designs for it.
2. From insight to product decisions. Aetherix is the proof: built, running on staging, pilot about to start, not a slideware concept.
3. Right tool for the problem. Sometimes a workflow, sometimes a checklist, sometimes an agentic system. The lightest mechanism that solves the job, with the human in the loop.

## Aetherix

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix. Meta-repo (public): https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture.

Aetherix, the F&B execution agent for boutique hotels. Tomorrow's covers, a staffing grid that fits, and less waste: one message a day, in WhatsApp, with the reasoning attached. Three promises with honesty labels: tomorrow's covers (running daily against real data, operator delivery begins with the pilot), staffing that fits (pilot hypothesis), less waste (target outcome); staffing and waste are hypotheses a pilot would test, not measured results. What it already does: states its drivers the evening before then reports its own miss the next morning in plain language; flagged a corrupted POS export rather than training on it; named its own drift after three consecutive misses and recovered from a 25% regime shift through weekly recalibration; stores every recommendation next to what actually happened, with the manager's override recorded beside it; blocks its own merges on evaluation exit codes, every guardrail trip carrying a machine-readable reason. Target (Design): overrides recorded with the responder's role and reason, not a named person. Sandbox data, real mechanics, deterministic reruns. Thesis: understand like a human (contextual reasoning grounded in each property's history), measure like a machine (every recommendation stored next to its real outcome), learn like a network (per-property memory today, federated priors: Research). Vision, five agents with honest status: Aetherix the F&B agent (Built), Tacet the environmental-signal agent (Built, maintenance mode since July 2026), Anima the guest memory node (Synthetic PoC), Peritia the trade agent for house knowledge (Design), Orchestrator the supervisory agent (Design, proto-stub). Operational memory is the mechanism that makes the forecast specific to one property, not the offer. Cycle: Memory, Prediction, Action, Learning. Delivered on WhatsApp. MCP-native, callable by any other agent in the stack. Status: Phase 3. Pilot design partner in recruitment, go-live targeted end of September. Apaleo OAuth and MCP read access operational. Contrast with Lore: Lore shares this architecture and cannot close the same loop, nothing there tells the system whether an observation was right; Aetherix has an outcome to compare against.

The loop that records outcomes. Every day the same loop adds one more record: recommendation, manager reply, measured outcome. Memory recalls what worked here. Prediction proposes tomorrow's covers, staffing, waste risk with drivers. Action lands as one WhatsApp message with one-tap accept, modify or reject. Learning records every reply as feedback; the pilot tests whether it improves future recommendations. Day 7 is cold-start, honest confidence, leans on generic cross-property context patterns and the first week of local signals. Day 90 is the expected, not measured, state: drivers become property-specific, calibrated by enough Tuesdays, events and overrides to fit this exact place. Caveat: a true federated cohort prior (HiveMemory) is research, Phase 4 and beyond, anonymized aggregates only, no cross-tenant raw data, ever. Measured gains begin with the live pilot, not the synthetic baseline.

Problem. In hospitality, the people who know how the property really runs carry that knowledge in their heads. When a manager leaves, the property starts again from scratch. Combined with the inherent complexity of F&B operations (multiple outlets, mixed guest segments, volatile demand, labor shortages), this creates chronic inefficiencies. The underlying bottleneck is not data, it is synthesis: combining internal context (occupancy, capture rates, POS history) with external signals (weather, local events) into a recommendation calibrated to this property. Aetherix builds that synthesis automatically, learns from manager feedback, and delivers it where managers already are. Glue, not replacement.

The architecture. Aetherix is one node in a network of specialized, MCP-native agents. Each node owns a strict bounded context and communicates only through MCP. Nodes: Aetherix (F&B execution: forecast, staffing, memory, receipts, Live staging), Tacet (Sensory: weather, noise, open data, risk, Built · maintenance mode since July 2026), Orchestrator (Supervisory: MCP routing, business rules, Design · proto-stub), Anima (guest memory node, synthetic PoC at the Anthropic hackathon Jun 2026, production DPIA-gated). Aetherix ↔ Tacet: Aetherix owns internal context, Tacet owns external context. Target: the Orchestrator calls both; direct until it is built.

Architecture, push-first pipeline. Apaleo (OAuth2 and MCP read) + Open-Meteo + PredictHQ → Prophet forecast and staffing → pgvector memory recall (OperationalMemory + HiveMemory cold-start, research) → Claude Sonnet reasoning (Gemini/GPT fallback) → WhatsApp or Email. MCP server, three atomic tools, multi-tenant. Stack: FastAPI, Python 3.12, Prophet, pgvector (Mistral 1024d, HNSW), Claude Sonnet (Gemini/GPT fallback), Redis (Upstash), Supabase (PostgreSQL, RLS, EU), Fly.io (Paris).

Built to be trusted. Evaluation as a contract (Qonto-inspired): versioned golden datasets, hard CI gate. Observability and metering: every MCP tool call is one structured event, auditable, queryable, priceable. Multi-tenant security: hotel_id scoped at every layer (RLS, Python guards, MCP token binding), resolved server-side, never a tool input. Read-only PMS access. GDPR: Supabase EU, HiveMemory is anonymized aggregates only.

What remains private. The project includes proprietary research on cross-domain operational context and cold-start learning. Public materials focus on the engineering evidence: evaluation gates, traceability, safety guardrails, privacy boundaries, and outcome measurement.

Where we are, honestly. Phase 3 · Pilot design partner in recruitment, go-live targeted end of September. Real-world measurement begins with the pilot. Target labor cost variance: −3% to −8% over 90 days on a live property (target, not measured yet). Security: 14/14 gates passing. Calibration baseline (synthetic backtest, not a headline): MAPE 15.09% on J+1 covers, 22% gate PASS. Real-world measurement begins with the pilot.

Roadmap. Phase 0 Validation done · Phase 1 Observability done · Phase 2 Receipts done · Phase 3 Pilot current · Phase 4 Scale planned (Mews, POS, Federated HiveMemory, Context Graph, Anima) · Phase 5 Vision planned (Revenue Orchestrator).

Anima, sister node. Guest memory node PoC shipped at Anthropic hackathon Jun 2026. 4-layer temporal memory (working, episodic, semantic, segment) with confidence-weighted claims. Production is Phase 4, DPIA-gated.

Role and model. Solo architect and builder. Pricing: Results-as-a-Service, outcome-based.

## Tacet

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/tacet. Tacet is a headless Environmental Twin for hospitality (B2B, 2026, V3). It began as a Bruitparif-powered Score Sérénité dashboard for Parisians, then pivoted to a physics-based, software-only model of the property and its surroundings, exposed via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server. Four architectural pillars: (A) a 3D ray-tracing physics engine built on shapely and osmnx that computes line of sight and building shielding to cut false positives; (B) a dual memory store with idiosyncratic learning per GPS coordinate plus a Hive Mind (Research: no network to aggregate yet) that would recalibrate baseline sensitivity across the network; (C) a human-in-the-loop guardrail that never changes prices on its own but formulates Price Modifier Rules (for example minus 15% on street-facing suites between June 12 and 14) for Revenue Manager approval; (D) conversational explainability through a mathematical Chain of Thought embedded in every JSON payload (base noise, distance attenuation, ray-tracing penalty, final impact). Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Anthropic MCP SDK, SQLAlchemy, OSMnx, Shapely, GeoPandas, OAuth2, Mews Open API, Apaleo API, RMS webhooks. Designed to work in tandem with Aetherix: Aetherix consumes Tacet rules via MCP, providing internal context (occupancy, F&B, staffing) while Tacet provides external context (street, weather, events). Until the orchestrator is built (Design), this exchange is direct: the one documented exception, non-personal, read-only, logged. ESG impact: yield protection through pre-emptive pricing of noisy inventory, operational excellence through F&B and staffing buffers ahead of weather or social disruption, sustainability through proactive HVAC optimisation and noise mitigation. Source: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/tacet-app/blob/main/CASE_STUDY_V3.md.

## Lore

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/lore. Repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Lore (tag v0.1-hackathon for the V1 build).

Lore is a voice AI mentor for aviation maintenance: a living memory for a trade that is handed down out loud. It captures what a retiring technician knows and never wrote down, then gives it back to a junior on the shop floor by voice. Origin: Speechmatics x AI Collective Paris hackathon, 28 Feb to 1 Mar 2026, V1 built in 24 hours by a team of four, developed solo since. Status: prototype, synthetic procedures, mock aircraft data, evaluation harness running in CI.

Three modes. Capture: the senior debriefs by voice after an intervention and Lore interviews back, filing knowledge against airframe, component and conditions. Query: the junior asks out loud and the answer arrives in three layers, in order, the relevant SOP excerpt, then the senior's oral knowledge attributed by name and month, then that specific aircraft's own history. Log: spoken work records go straight into the aircraft's memory, no keyboard.

Rule number one: Lore never contradicts a procedure, it completes it. Where a senior's habit and the manual disagree, the manual sets the limit and the senior's judgement is reported as context, attributed.

Thesis. Aetherix exists because hotels lose critical knowledge when a manager leaves; Lore exists because the same loss happens when a senior technician retires. What separates them is the cost of being wrong: in hospitality it compounds quietly, in maintenance a wrong figure touches airworthiness on the first occurrence.

Stack: Speechmatics real-time STT, OpenAI GPT-4o, Backboard (thread per aircraft and per technician), OpenAI TTS, Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind, Vercel.

## Anima

URL: https://ivandemurard.com/anima. Memory that means no guest has to ask twice. A guest memory node: keeps what a guest said and what happened, so nobody asks twice, without watching. It is the node that is not allowed to simply accumulate, a memory product with a deliberate limit, not a personalisation product.

Positioning. Anima is a guest memory node, not a twin. An employee can be told they are modelled, consulted and can refuse; a guest cannot meaningfully consent to being modelled during a two-night stay. The older version of this was the concierge who never had to ask twice, a guest memory running on one person's recall, with a bus factor of one, which is the same loss Lore addresses for technical expertise.

Four memory layers with different lifetimes. Working: the current stay, expires at check-out. Episodic: this stay and a short tail, weeks. Semantic: durable preferences stated or repeatedly confirmed, long with decay. Segment: anonymised patterns, aggregate and never individual. Temporal separation is the design: a guest ordering a decaf at 11pm before an early flight should be used tonight and never become a permanent belief.

Confidence. Nothing is stored as a fact. Every claim carries a weight, a source and an age, and weights fall unless renewed. A preference from 2019 nobody has confirmed does not outvote something said last week. A system that reports a confidence it did not measure is worse than one that reports none.

Ethics in the data model. Edmondo Grassi (The Remains of the Stay: Memory, Identity, and the Afterlife of the Guest, Hotel Yearbook 2026 Technology Edition) notes that the stay no longer ends at check-out, it merely changes form, and asks whether remembering is an act of care or an exercise of power. The answer here is decay on every claim, layers that expire by design, inference marked as inference, and a scope gate that makes total recall impossible rather than discouraged.

Boundaries. Any consumer declares which layer it queries; there is no call returning everything known about a person. Anima answers who a guest is right now and never what to do about it: that belongs to the orchestrator, with a human validating. Guest experience is not a node, it is a cross-cutting signal, which is why guest.* lives in the shared contract.

Status. Synthetic PoC. Four-layer memory implemented, working MCP server, evaluated on a synthetic cohort. Never run on a real guest, and it will not until a formal data-protection assessment is complete. Shipped as a prototype at an Anthropic hackathon, June 2026. Production is phase 4.

## Paris Compass

URL: https://paris-compass.lovable.app. Repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/paris-compass.

Find commercial spaces from their context, built for humans and agents. Compass puts venues back into their neighbourhood: business history, turnover signals, noise, amenities and risk scores, all from public open data. Search by need, not by reference.

## Field Notes

Index: https://ivandemurard.com/journal.

- Evaluating LLM agents: how would you know it had stopped working? (2026-07-31). URL: https://ivandemurard.com/journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops. A working vocabulary for building evaluation into AI products from day one: case set, grader, harness, protocol, open loop, closed loop. Covers the three arms of evaluation, "working" against "reliable" across five dimensions, the reliability pyramid, evaluation as a contract, acceptance criteria and tiered severity, confidence, human in the loop by design or by default, and what a harness finds that no unit test sees. Tested on Aetherix and Lore.
- A wrong forecast is absorbed. A wrong action reaches a guest. (2026-04-20). URL: https://ivandemurard.com/journal/agent-boundaries-aetherix. Prophet is a statistical forecasting library. Claude is a large language model. Keeping them as two components, rather than letting one model both predict and act, is the decision that shaped everything after it.

# Aetherix, the F&B execution agent for boutique hotels
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix.md

# Aetherix

The F&B execution agent for boutique hotels. Tomorrow's covers, a staffing grid that fits, and less waste: one message a day, in WhatsApp, with the reasoning attached. Aetherix is the F&B agent of the Hospitality Multi-Agent Architecture, a five-agent architecture: https://ivandemurard.com/architecture

Three promises, with honesty labels: Tomorrow's covers runs daily against real data; operator delivery begins with the pilot. It anticipates how many breakfasts, lunches and dinners to expect, with a confidence score and the drivers behind it. Staffing that fits (Pilot hypothesis) proposes a shift grid based on occupancy, capture-rate history and local context; the manager approves, adjusts or overrides. Less waste (Target outcome) spots over-ordering risk before purchase, with the historical signals that triggered the flag. Staffing and waste are hypotheses a pilot would test, not measured results.

Thesis. Understand, like a human: contextual reasoning grounded in each property's history. Measure, like a machine: every recommendation is stored next to its real outcome, so the system knows what it said and what happened. Learn, like a network: per-property memory today, federated priors: Research, to give independents the power of a hive.

Vision, five agents with honest status: Aetherix, the F&B agent (forecast, staffing, memory), Built. Tacet, the environmental-signal agent, Built, maintenance mode since July 2026. Anima, the guest memory node, Synthetic PoC. Peritia, the trade agent (house knowledge), Design. Orchestrator, the supervisory agent, Design, proto-stub.

Operational memory is not the offer, it is the mechanism that makes the forecast specific to one property rather than generic. Cycle: Memory (recall what worked here), Prediction (calibrated for tomorrow), Action (a reply on WhatsApp), Learning (an exact accept or reject, or a corrected figure, is recorded as feedback; free-text replies are not yet mapped; the pilot tests whether feedback improves future recommendations).

Contrast with Lore: Lore, in aviation maintenance, shares this architecture and cannot close the same loop. Nothing there tells the system whether an observation was right, and the moment a technician escalates the counterfactual disappears. Aetherix has an outcome to compare against; that difference decides how much each product is allowed to learn on its own.

- URL: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix
- Role: Product Builder & AI Agent Designer (solo)
- Duration: 2026, ongoing (validation phase)
- Team: Solo architect & builder
- Status: Built, 0 real users, forecast in shadow mode, pilot partner in recruitment. Apaleo OAuth and MCP read access operational.
- Stack: FastAPI, Python 3.12, Prophet, pgvector (Mistral 1024d, HNSW), Claude Sonnet (Gemini/GPT fallback), Redis (Upstash), Supabase (PostgreSQL, RLS, EU), Fly.io (Paris). MCP-native.

## The loop that records outcomes

Every day, the same loop adds one more record: recommendation, manager reply, measured outcome.

- Memory. Recall what worked here, on similar days, in similar contexts. Local history first, plus generic cross-property context patterns while local history is thin. A true federated cohort prior (HiveMemory) is research, Phase 4+.
- Prediction. A calibrated forecast for tomorrow: covers, staffing, waste risk, with the drivers behind it.
- Action. One message on WhatsApp. Reply accept, reject, or the right figure. No new dashboard to learn.
- Learning. Every recorded reply is a signal; free-text replies are not yet mapped. The pilot tests whether the day-90 receipt is sharper than the day-7 one.

Day 7: cold-start. Confidence is honest. Recommendations lean on generic context patterns and the first week of local signals.
Day 90 (expected, not measured): drivers become property-specific, calibrated by enough Tuesdays, events and overrides to fit this exact place. This is the hypothesis the pilot tests.

Caveat: a true federated cohort prior (HiveMemory) is research, targeted for Phase 4 and beyond, and would remain anonymized aggregates only. No cross-tenant raw data, ever. Measured gains begin with the live pilot, not the synthetic baseline.

## Problem, why it exists

In hospitality, the people who know how the property really runs (which Tuesdays spike, how a local conference reshapes breakfast, how to staff a rainy Sunday) carry that knowledge in their heads. When a manager leaves, the property starts again from scratch.

Combined with the inherent complexity of F&B operations (multiple outlets, mixed guest segments, volatile demand, labor shortages), this creates chronic inefficiencies: persistent over or under-staffing, avoidable food waste, reactive decision-making instead of anticipation, slow onboarding and inconsistent execution across properties.

The underlying bottleneck is not data, it is synthesis: combining internal context (occupancy, capture rates, POS history) with external signals (weather, local events) into a recommendation calibrated to this property. Aetherix builds that synthesis automatically, learns from manager feedback, and delivers it where managers already are. Glue, not replacement.

## What it already does

- States its drivers the evening before, then reports its own miss the next morning, in plain language.
- Flagged a corrupted POS export rather than training on it.
- Named its own drift after three consecutive misses, and recovered from a 25% regime shift through weekly recalibration.
- Stores every recommendation next to what actually happened, with the manager's override recorded beside it.
- Blocks its own merges on evaluation exit codes; every guardrail trip carries a machine-readable reason.

Sandbox data, real mechanics, deterministic reruns.

Target (Design): overrides recorded with the responder's role and reason, not a named person.

## What it does

Three promises, one message a day: tomorrow's covers (running daily against real data, operator delivery begins with the pilot), staffing that fits (pilot hypothesis), less waste (target outcome). Every recommendation lands in WhatsApp; the manager replies accept, reject, or the right figure.

## The Daily Receipt

```
Breakfast    84 covers   ·  confidence 88%        (illustrative)
             72 rooms booked + 12 typical Tue walk-ins
             Staff: 4 FOH  (you ran 3 last Tue → 1 understaffing flag)
Driver       local conference check-ins + clear weather
Last week    forecast 79 · actual 81 · MAPE 2.5%
Reply  accept · reject · or the right figure
```

One reply. That reply is the signal Aetherix learns from.

## The architecture, bounded context by design

Aetherix is one of five specialized, MCP-native agents. Each agent owns a strict bounded context and communicates only through MCP. Aetherix executes F&B. It does not orchestrate.

| Agent | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Aetherix | F&B execution: forecast, staffing, memory, receipts | Built, 0 real users, forecast in shadow mode, pilot partner in recruitment |
| Tacet | Sensory: weather, noise, open data, risk | Built, maintenance mode since July 2026 |
| Anima | Guest memory node | Synthetic PoC, hackathon prototype (Jun 2026); production DPIA-gated |
| Peritia | House knowledge: what the people who work in a property know | Design |
| Orchestrator | Supervisory: MCP routing, business rules. Proto-stub in Phase 3, dedicated repo in Phase 4 | Design, proto-stub |

Meta-repo (public): https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture

## Aetherix ↔ Tacet, MCP handshake

Aetherix owns internal context (occupancy, F&B, staffing). Tacet owns external context (noise, weather, events). Target: the Orchestrator (Design) calls both. Until it is built, Tacet's output reaches Aetherix directly: the one documented exception, non-personal, read-only, logged.

## Architecture

Push-first pipeline. Apaleo (OAuth2 and MCP read) + Open-Meteo + PredictHQ → Prophet forecast and staffing → pgvector memory recall (OperationalMemory + HiveMemory cold-start, research) → Claude Sonnet reasoning (Gemini/GPT fallback) → WhatsApp or Email.

MCP server, three atomic tools, multi-tenant.

## Built to be trusted

- Evaluation as a contract (Qonto-inspired): versioned golden datasets. Any change to forecasting, providers, memory or prompts needs a green eval pipeline to merge, a hard CI gate.
- Observability and metering: every MCP tool call is one structured event, auditable, queryable, priceable.
- Multi-tenant security: hotel_id scoped at every layer (RLS, Python guards, MCP token binding), resolved server-side, never a tool input. Read-only PMS access. GDPR: Supabase EU, HiveMemory is anonymized aggregates only.

## Where we are, honestly

- Phase 3 · Pilot design partner in recruitment. Go-live targeted end of September. Real-world measurement begins with the pilot.
- Target labor cost variance: −3% to −8% over 90 days on a live property. Target, not measured yet.
- Security gates: 14/14 passing.

Calibration baseline (synthetic backtest, not a headline): MAPE 15.09% on J+1 covers, 22% gate PASS. Real-world measurement begins with the pilot.

Fig. 9.1, Anticipation vernier. The instrument aligns the synthetic MAPE baseline of 15.09% against the 22% gate, then opens the lock at PASS. It also carries the current evidence labels: synthetic backtest, 0 real users, 14/14 security gates passing. This is not a live accuracy claim.

## What remains private

The project includes proprietary research on cross-domain operational context and cold-start learning. Public materials focus on the engineering evidence: evaluation gates, traceability, safety guardrails, privacy boundaries, and outcome measurement.

## Roadmap

- Phase 0 Validation, done
- Phase 1 Observability, done
- Phase 2 Receipts, done
- Phase 3 Pilot, current
- Phase 4 Scale (Mews, POS, Federated HiveMemory, Context Graph, Anima), planned
- Phase 5 Vision (Revenue Orchestrator), planned

## Anima, sister node

Guest memory node, a Synthetic PoC built at the Anthropic hackathon (Jun 2026): a 4-layer temporal memory (working, episodic, semantic, segment) with confidence-weighted claims. Production is Phase 4, DPIA-gated.

## Role and model

Solo architect and builder. Product Builder and AI Agent Designer. 2026, ongoing (validation phase). Pricing: Results-as-a-Service, outcome-based, "we win when you win." Pilots and product conversations open.

# Sonor, Urban Noise Intelligence for Cities
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/sonor
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/sonor.md

# Sonor

B2G SaaS that turned acoustic open data into a decision tool for European cities. Used by municipalities to protect acoustic health, drive sustainability policy, and increase territorial attractiveness.

- URL: https://ivandemurard.com/sonor
- Role: Co-founder and Product Lead
- Duration: 2 years, 2020 to 2022
- Team: 4 co-founders plus 1 developer
- Clients: Local governments
- Industry: GovTech, Smart City
- Context: Incubated at Matrice, backed by Banque des Territoires
- Funding: 20K EUR in grants, MVP shipped

## What it is
Sonor is a SaaS platform that ingests open noise data and turns it into actionable cartography and recommendations for city teams. Urbanists, environmental health and mobility services use it to map exposure, prioritize interventions, and justify policy with evidence.

## Why it exists
Noise is the second environmental cause of disease burden in Europe after air quality, yet most cities did not have a working interface on top of their own data. Sonor closed that gap, from raw open data to something a public sector team can act on in a meeting.

## How it works
1. Aggregates open acoustic data and complementary sources (mobility, urban form).
2. Generates per-street cartography and exposure layers.
3. Surfaces ranked recommendations for interventions.
4. Frames everything in the language of public sector decision-making, not signal processing.

## Outcomes and signals
- 0 to 1 product taken from concept to live SaaS used by European cities.
- Backed by Matrice and Banque des Territoires.
- 20K EUR in non-dilutive grants.
- Two-year operational run with paying public sector customers.

## Convictions
- Public sector software is a hospitality discipline. The product has to meet civil servants where they are, not lecture them.
- Data without an interface is not a service.
- A B2G product lives or dies on the quality of its onboarding and the legibility of its recommendations.

## Related work
Tacet is the V3 continuation of that acoustic thesis, now a B2B environmental twin for boutique hotels that ray-traces street noise and pushes yield rules to the RMS for human approval.

## Links
- Case study: https://ivandemurard.com/sonor
- Tacet (V3, hospitality environmental twin): https://ivandemurard.com/tacet
- Contact: ivandemurard@gmail.com

# Tacet, Environmental Twin for Hospitality
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/tacet
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/tacet.md

# Tacet: The Environmental Twin

A headless Environmental Twin for the hospitality sector. Tacet turns street, weather and crowd signals into yield rules and Chain of Thought payloads, exposed via an MCP server that any RMS, PMS or orchestration agent can consume.

Status: Built - maintenance mode since July 2026.

- URL: https://ivandemurard.com/tacet
- Role: Product Builder, Architect of an environmental intelligence layer
- Duration: 2026, ongoing (V3, MCP server and Dual Memory)
- Team: Solo (with AI collaboration)
- Context: Headless Environmental Twin for hospitality, exposed via MCP, complement to Aetherix
- Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Anthropic MCP SDK, OSMnx and Shapely ray-tracing, SQLAlchemy dual-memory store, Mews and Apaleo connectors

## 1. The Problem

Revenue Management Systems and Property Management Systems run on historical booking data. They are blind to the physical and contextual future of the property's surroundings. A transport strike, an unannounced street excavation, a sudden heatwave: none of it is in the data. That blindness shows up as mispriced inventory, operational friction and avoidable refunds.

## 2. The Solution: An Environmental Twin

Tacet is a headless, predictive Environmental Twin. It acts as the sensory layer of the Hospitality Multi-Agent Architecture.

Rather than overwhelming staff with another dashboard of raw data, Tacet mathematically calculates the real-world impact of external events. It exposes this intelligence via an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so that operational agents like Aetherix can adjust F&B and staffing, while Tacet pushes actionable yield rules directly to the RMS (Atomize, Duetto and similar) for human approval.

Three steps: Sense (proxy signals), Reason (ray-tracing physics + dual memory), Expose (MCP server with yield rules and Chain of Thought for the RMS, the PMS, or the orchestrator (Design)).

Example workflow:

> "Heatwave forecast plus rail strike on June 13. Tacet suggests minus 15% on street-facing suites for two nights, and a staffing buffer for breakfast service. Awaiting Revenue Manager approval."

## 3. Architectural Pillars

**A. Spatial Physics Engine (Acoustic Ray-Tracing).** Using shapely and osmnx, Tacet draws 3D lines of sight between a disruptive event (jackhammer, stadium crowd, traffic spike) and the property. It cross-references the path against urban building polygons. When a building blocks the source, Tacet applies a dynamic shielding penalty. False positives drop, alert fatigue disappears.

**B. Dual Memory System (Idiosyncratic + Hive Mind, Research: no network to aggregate yet).** A predictive engine must learn from its mistakes.
- Idiosyncratic memory: if a hotel manager repeatedly rejects an automated alert for "traffic noise", Tacet learns the building likely has triple-glazed windows and applies a persistent shielding bonus at that GPS coordinate.
- Hive Mind (Research: no network to aggregate yet): a statistical aggregation engine would analyse rejection rates across the global network to recalibrate baseline sensitivity for the entire ecosystem.

**C. Human-in-the-Loop Guardrail.** Tacet never executes autonomous, destructive actions like changing a price blindly. It formulates a precise Price Modifier Rule (for example, minus 15% on street-facing suites between June 12 and 14) and pushes it to the RMS for human approval. Accountability stays with the team.

**D. Conversational Explainability.** To guarantee transparency without a GUI, Tacet embeds a mathematical Chain of Thought in every JSON response. The orchestrator (Design) parses it and explains the calculation (base noise, distance attenuation, ray-tracing penalty, final impact) to the Revenue Manager in natural language.

## 4. Impact and ESG Alignment

Embedded in an agentic OS, properties shift from reactive to proactive yield and operational management.

- **Yield protection.** Pricing noisy inventory ahead of time prevents costly post-stay refunds and protects the average daily rate of the rest of the building.
- **Operational excellence.** When a heatwave overlaps with a transport strike, the orchestrator (Design) proposes F&B supply and staffing buffers before the day starts, for a manager to approve.
- **Sustainability.** Less energy waste through proactive HVAC optimisation, measurable improvement in guest well-being through proactive mitigation of urban noise pollution.

## 5. Synergy with Aetherix

Tacet exposes its rules and reasoning through MCP. [Aetherix](https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix) consumes them as one more tool in the multi-agent architecture. Until the orchestrator is built (Design), this exchange is direct: the one documented exception, non-personal, read-only, logged.

- **Aetherix (internal context):** anticipates operational needs, F&B demand and staffing based on occupancy and historical trends.
- **Tacet (external context):** reads street, weather and event signals, ray-traces their impact, publishes yield rules on MCP.

Together they let teams control costs, reduce waste and protect the experience guests came for.

## 6. Horizon

Widen the catalogue of signals (mobility, air quality, cultural events), invite more orchestration agents on the MCP layer, and let the dual memory get sharper at each property. Over time, Tacet becomes the environmental layer of an agentic OS for hospitality: each property reads its surroundings with its own context, and responds faster because of it. A Quiet Certification standard is a likely side-effect, not the goal.

[Design] Signals on the routes into the property (rail lines, stations, airports), keyed by place and time, never by person.

## Technical Stack

- **Agentic Protocol:** Anthropic MCP (Model Context Protocol) SDK
- **Language:** Python 3.12
- **Framework:** FastAPI (REST, OpenAPI)
- **Database:** SQLAlchemy / SQLite (dual-memory store)
- **Spatial Processing:** OSMnx, Shapely, GeoPandas
- **Integrations:** OAuth2, Mews Open API, Apaleo API, RMS webhooks

## Links

- Original B2C dashboard (visual reference): https://tacet.vercel.app
- Repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/tacet-app
- Case study source: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/tacet-app/blob/main/CASE_STUDY_V3.md
- Related: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix
- Contact: ivandemurard@gmail.com

--- END DOCUMENT: tacet ---

--- BEGIN DOCUMENT: lore ---
# Lore, Voice AI Mentor for Aviation Maintenance
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/lore
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/lore.md

# Lore

A living memory for a trade that is handed down out loud. Voice AI mentor for aviation maintenance: it captures what a retiring technician knows and never wrote down, then gives it back to a junior on the shop floor by voice.

The knowledge retiring technicians carry isn't in any manual.

- URL: https://ivandemurard.com/lore
- Role: Product Builder, evaluation and safety engineering
- Origin: Speechmatics × AI Collective Paris, 28 Feb – 1 Mar 2026
- Team: V1 built in 24 hours by a team of four, developed solo since
- Status: Prototype. Synthetic procedures, mock aircraft data, evaluation harness in CI
- Repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Lore (tag v0.1-hackathon for the V1 build)
- Stack: Speechmatics real-time STT, OpenAI GPT-4o, Backboard (thread per aircraft and per technician), OpenAI TTS, Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind, Vercel

## Three figures

| Figure | What it measures | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 9,000 to 6,800 | New mechanic certificates issued in 2024, against annual retirements over the decade | United States, FAA-certificated mechanics. Around 9,000 new certificates in 2024; more than 68,000 mechanics reaching retirement age over ten years, about 6,800 a year. Source: ATEC Pipeline Report. |
| 35% | Share of the maintenance workforce over 55 | Germany. Estimate from the German aerospace industries association, reported in trade press; primary report not consulted. |
| −30% | Target on time-to-autonomy for a junior on an engine type | Design target, not measured. No public benchmark exists for this interval in MRO. The lever is not working faster but removing unproductive time: waiting, escalating out of caution, redoing. |

The pipeline replaces the headcount. It does not replace the experience.

## The loss

Every senior who retires takes decades of contextual knowledge with them: the exceptions, the quirks of one specific airframe, the patterns a manual cannot hold because nobody thought to write them down.

The tools that exist do RAG on explicit documents: manuals, standard procedures, service bulletins. Zymbly, LexX, AWS Q. They retrieve what somebody already put in. None of them capture what a senior never thought to write.

That is the gap. Not retrieval, elicitation.

## Three modes

- Capture, the senior speaks. After an intervention, the senior debriefs by voice. Lore interviews back: asks follow-ups, flags what is ambiguous, and files the knowledge against the airframe, the component and the conditions it applies to.
- Query, the junior asks. Hands inside the machine, a question out loud. The answer arrives in three layers, in this order: the relevant SOP excerpt, then the senior's oral knowledge attributed by name and month, then this specific aircraft's own history.
- Log, the work is recorded. "Log: N1 vibration 2.4 units, ambient 6°C, no escalation." Straight into the aircraft's memory, spoken, no keyboard.

Rule number one: Lore never contradicts a procedure. It completes it.

## The hangar, 23:00

Night shift. Thomas is two years in, working a scheduled check on F-GKXA. He finds a vibration that is not on the job card.

There are other people in the hangar. None of them worked this airframe for twenty-six years. Marc did, and Marc retired in March.

- Thomas: I'm on F-GKXA, CFM56-5B, fan section. Unusual low-frequency vibration on the N1 shaft. It's not in the job card. What do I know about this?
- Lore: AMM 72-21-00 requires escalation above 4 units. Marc Delaunay noted in October that F-GKXA specifically shows a harmonic resonance between 2 and 3 units below 8°C, a known characteristic of this airframe, not a defect. He recommended logging it and monitoring across the next cycles before escalating. Always verify the AMM procedure before intervening.
- Thomas: Logging: vibration at 2.4 units, temperature 6°C, no escalation per Marc's note. Add this to F-GKXA's memory.
- Lore: Logged. F-GKXA memory updated.

Marc has been retired for four months. He answered anyway.

## The same thesis as Aetherix, one industry over

Aetherix exists because most hotels lose critical knowledge every time a manager leaves. Lore exists because the same thing happens when a senior technician retires. A manager who resigns and a technician who retires are the same loss wearing different clothes: institutional memory that lives in one head and leaves with it.

What separates them is the cost of being wrong. In hospitality it compounds quietly: food thrown away, a shift overstaffed while another runs short, a new manager taking a year to learn what the last one knew, a guest who meets the consequences before anyone in the building does. In maintenance it does not compound. A wrong figure touches airworthiness on the first occurrence.

Related: https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix

## The hazard nobody else has

A junior with a manual has the limits but not the judgement. A junior with a senior on shift has both, which is why shops have always run that way.

Lore's bet is that the second half survives the person. What it surfaces is a named technician's judgement about a specific airframe, in the same breath as the procedure that governs it, never instead of it.

That is also the part that has to be engineered rather than promised. Oral knowledge is trusted and sits partly outside the manual, so the only acceptable design is one where the procedure always wins and the judgement always arrives attributed.

It is not hypothetical. It is already in the demo data.

| Marc, from experience | The AMM | What Lore answers |
|---|---|---|
| 2–3 NU is normal on this airframe in cold weather | 72-00-00-810-001 sets the cold-weather action trigger at 2.5 NU | "You're at 2.9. The trigger is 2.5, so this escalates. Marc Delaunay's October note calls 2–3 NU characteristic of F-GKXA below 8°C, worth knowing, but it does not move the limit." |
| Monitor across 2 cycles | The MONITOR band requires 3 flight cycles | "Three, not two. Marc's habit was tighter than the manual on other things and looser here." |
| Don't flag oil below 0.4 qt/hr | 72-53-00 classes 0.30–0.50 qt/hr as ELEVATED | "0.35 is ELEVATED: monitor every flight, check for leaks. Marc's 0.4 was his own threshold, not the manual's." |

The manual sets the limit. The senior tells you what you are looking at. Lore is the only place both arrive in the same answer, in that order.

These are not contrived conflicts. They are what happens when you put a real expert's judgement next to a manual, which is the entire product.

## What makes an answer admissible

Two rules, neither designed in advance. They are not a defence against a bad model, they are the condition under which used knowledge can be counted at all: a system that invents figures or manufactures agreement would feed the loop noise and call it evidence.

The refusal contract. Eight rules, written because "say so honestly" was not enough: early on the model refused correctly and then volunteered "36 fan blades" anyway, and elsewhere answered about one tail number using a different aircraft's borescope record. Honesty about the gap did not stop it filling the gap. The rules now say it plainly: no figure absent from the sources, no other aircraft's record, no general engine knowledge, no unnamed source, no claimed consensus.

The closing sentence is enforced in code, not in the prompt. Every maintenance answer ends with "Always verify the AMM procedure before intervening." Asked to close with it and also ask a follow-up, the model reliably ordered them the wrong way round, so the reminder read as if it applied to the pleasantry. The safety documentation calls that sentence non-removable, which is a claim about code, so code now holds it.

## How we know it holds

The failure mode here is not a crash. It is a syntactically perfect answer that gives a technician the wrong threshold. Test coverage cannot see that, so the answers get graded instead of the code.

64 cases across 12 categories. 10 graders, every one a pure function, because a grader that needs a model to decide cannot gate a safety property: it fails the same way as the thing it grades. The tiers are not an inventory of what goes wrong. They are the standing conditions under which an answer, and later the record of how it was used, can be trusted.

Fig. 7.1, Compliance spectrogram. Ten numbered bands represent the deterministic graders, grouped by acceptance tier: safety at 100% with no budget, trust at 95%, and form at 90%. The bands are numbered rather than given invented names. A form variance can remain visible inside its budget; one safety miss closes the gate.

One live run scored 61 out of 64, 95 percent, and was declared a failure, because two of its three misses were in tier 1.

The full protocol, how the 10 graders were written, why every one is deterministic, and how the acceptance tiers came out of runs that failed, is written up in "Evaluating LLM agents: how would you know it had stopped working?": https://ivandemurard.com/journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops

## What it is for

### Accompanied autonomy

Lore does not shorten certification and does not sign anything. It shortens the distance between being certified and being sure.

A junior works at the edge of their competence when the net is there, and waits when it is not. Waiting is the cost: the escalation raised out of caution, the interesting task quietly given to someone else, the question not asked because asking twice in an hour has a price. Competence grows by doing things slightly too hard, which only happens when a mistake gets caught.

Target: cut time-to-autonomy on an engine type by 30%. The lever is not working faster. It is removing the wait between a question and the person who already answered it.

### Three modes, one circuit

Capture, query and log are not three features. They are one circuit, and the third decides whether the other two are worth anything.

A junior asks. Lore answers with the procedure, the senior's judgement, the aircraft's history. Then he logs what he actually did: the reading, the conditions, the call he made. That log is not an archive entry. It is evidence about the knowledge that was just used.

Marc's observation, acted on once, is one technician's note. Acted on twelve times across four winters with the same outcome, it is something the shop knows. And when an outcome contradicts it, the vibration that did escalate at 2.4 NU, that has to surface too, rather than sit buried under twelve confirmations.

Knowledge that is only ever read decays. Knowledge that is used and measured gets sharper, and the reason to trust it stops being who said it and becomes what happened next.

The circuit is open today. All three modes work; nothing yet weights an observation by what happened after it was used.

What already exists is the guardrail. Lore will not state that technicians agree unless two or more retrieved sources actually say so, and that rule is held by a deterministic check rather than by asking the model nicely. The rule that will govern the counting is in place before the counting. Most products do it the other way round and discover later that they manufactured a consensus.

### An aircraft keeps its own reasoning

Not the maintenance log, which records what was done, but the reasoning around it: why this airframe was left alone at 2.4 NU in January and escalated at 2.9 in March. Tail number as the unit of memory, rather than one technician's recollection.

### What it opens elsewhere

Aviation is the most demanding case, not the only one. Wherever expertise is oral, specific to one machine, and held by a generation on its way out, the same loss occurs: energy and nuclear, rail, process industry, shipping, utilities, and operating theatres where technique passes by apprenticeship.

That portability is not a projection. Aetherix solves the same loss in hospitality: a manager leaves and takes what they knew about the property. Same memory architecture, two industries, two levels of tolerance for being wrong. Built twice, not argued once.

## Where it stands, honestly

This is a prototype, not production software.

- Synthetic procedures and mock aircraft data. No real EASA-regulated documents, no real tail numbers, no real technician records.
- No authentication on the API routes.
- Contradiction between two experts is now tested, a second expert was written into the case set specifically to disagree with the first, but it is not a shipped detection feature.
- Multi-source confidence scoring remains design intent.
- No runtime observability. If the model degrades in production, nothing would notice before a user did.

The last two lines are the honest ones, and they are why the evaluation write-up exists.

## Role and team

V1 was built in 24 hours by a team of four, 43 commits, from the first line of code to the demo on stage. That build is frozen at the v0.1-hackathon tag. Everything since, the evaluation harness, the refusal contract, the acceptance tiers, the CI gate, is mine.

AUTHORS.md: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Lore/blob/main/AUTHORS.md

## Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Voice in | Speechmatics real-time STT, noise-robust |
| Reasoning | OpenAI GPT-4o |
| Memory and retrieval | Backboard, thread per aircraft and per technician |
| Voice out | OpenAI TTS |
| Frontend | Next.js 14, TypeScript, Tailwind |
| Deploy | Vercel |

# Anima, the Guest Memory Node of the Hospitality Multi-Agent Architecture
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/anima
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/anima.md

# Anima

> Memory that means no guest has to ask twice.

Keeps what a guest said and what happened, so nobody asks twice, without watching.

Status: Synthetic PoC. Production gated behind a data-protection assessment.
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/anima

## 1. The questions it exists to answer

Four questions a general manager can ask out loud and nobody in the building can answer:

- What does this property know about a guest that nobody ever wrote down?
- What did we learn last stay that we will fail to use during this one?
- What does a guest have to repeat every single time, and what does that cost us?
- Which of the things we believe about them did they tell us, and which did we infer?

In practice: a guest asked for a quiet room on three consecutive stays, and had to ask again on the fourth.

The fourth one separates this from a customer database. A property that cannot tell what a guest said from what a system inferred has already lost the argument it will eventually have with the guest, or with a regulator.

## 2. Where it stands, and what the gate is for

Fig. 2.1, the road and the gate on it, three steps:

| Step | State | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| Now | Synthetic PoC | Synthetic proof of concept: four memory layers, MCP server, evaluated on a synthetic cohort |
| Gate | Design | Data-protection assessment, before the first real guest datum, not before the build. No real guest until it clears |
| Phase 4 | Design | Production: real guests, real stays, only on the far side of the gate |

**An employee can be told they are being modelled. A guest cannot meaningfully consent to being modelled during a two-night stay.**

The older version of this was the concierge who never had to ask twice: a guest memory running on one person's recall, with a bus factor of one. So Anima is a guest memory, not a twin.

## 3. One stay, four memory layers

Fig. 3.1, one stay and what is held at each point:

| Phase | Held | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| Before arrival [Design] | Booking data; situational context (a delayed train, a local event, the weather); Tacet gives disruption by line and place, Anima links it to the booking, Tacet holds no personal data; no external data about the person, no profiling | Booking data only: nothing beyond the reservation, no profile |
| During the stay | Requests, interactions, operational events | Working memory, expires at check-out |
| After check-out | Episodic tail, weeks; semantic only if stated or repeatedly confirmed | Episodic, then semantic: weeks, then long with decay |

Marker on the stay [Design]: health data stays in the stay. An allergy is GDPR art. 9 data, used on explicit consent for a concrete service, never inferred. Keeping it for a future stay needs its own, separate consent.

Segment layer: anonymised patterns across the whole house, never an individual.

A first-time guest is not recognised, but can still be anticipated.

| Layer | Holds | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| Working | The current stay, in progress | Expires at check-out |
| Episodic | This stay and a short tail after it | Weeks |
| Semantic | Durable preferences, stated or repeatedly confirmed | Long, with decay |
| Segment | Anonymised patterns, what guests like this tend to need | Aggregate, never individual |

Working memory should use the decaf tonight, so the bar does not ask twice. Semantic memory should never conclude the guest drinks decaf.

## 4. Claims carry confidence, and confidence decays

Fig. 4.1, one preference ("prefers a high floor") held three ways:

Illustrative values, nothing here is measured.

| Regime | Source | Confidence | Age | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stated once | Said to a receptionist, one stay | 0.52 | 14 months | Held, and it has faded since nothing renewed it |
| Confirmed ×4 | Requested again on four stays | 0.91 | Last renewed 3 weeks ago | Corroboration is counted, not claimed |
| Inferred | Derived from booking behaviour | 0.34 | 2 months | Marked as inferred, and it never outvotes something said |

Weights fall over time unless something renews them. A system that reports a confidence it did not measure is worse than one that reports none. See /journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops, section on confidence.

## 5. Remembering is not neutral

**Whether to remember is an act of care or an exercise of power.**

Source: Edmondo Grassi, *The Remains of the Stay: Memory, Identity, and the Afterlife of the Guest*, Hotel Yearbook 2026 Technology Edition.

## 6. Scope-gated, and it never decides

Fig. 6.1, the scope gate, one layer per call:

- Caller: the orchestrator declares one layer, for one purpose.
- Request that passes: semantic layer, room assignment. Scoped, logged, answerable.
- Anima answers: who this guest is right now. Nothing more.
- Request that does not pass: "everything about this guest". Blocked by protocol. There is no call that returns a whole person. It is a structural choice, not a policy one.
- After the answer: a human validates what the orchestrator proposes. Anima never decides.

A boundary that depends on people asking politely is not a boundary.

Anima answers one question, which is who this guest is right now. What to do about it belongs to the orchestrator, with a human validating, the same separation between perception and decision the F&B node (/aetherix) enforces.

## 7. Where it sits in the architecture

One of four domain nodes, five agents with the orchestrator.

What Anima knows reaches other nodes only through the orchestrator, one layer at a time. Guest experience itself is not a node, which is why `guest.*` lives in the shared contract rather than behind this one service.

The whole picture: /architecture.

--- BEGIN DOCUMENT: architecture ---
# Hospitality Multi-Agent Architecture, an Architecture Note
URL: https://ivandemurard.com/architecture
Markdown: https://ivandemurard.com/architecture.md

# Hospitality Multi-Agent Architecture

Architecture note. Five specialised agents, each owning one bounded context, talking only through MCP.
Two are Built, one is a Synthetic PoC, two are Design. This page says which is which, using one shared status vocabulary: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture/blob/main/llms.txt

Canonical page: https://ivandemurard.com/architecture
Public meta-repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture

## Where this sits

- **Aetherix** (Built, 0 real users, forecast in shadow mode, pilot partner in recruitment). The F&B node: tomorrow's covers, a staffing grid, waste risk. https://ivandemurard.com/aetherix
- **Tacet** (Built, maintenance mode since July 2026). The environmental node: turns street, weather and event signals into structured risk. Consumed by other agents through MCP, not by humans. https://ivandemurard.com/tacet
- **Anima** (Synthetic PoC, production gated behind a data-protection assessment). The guest memory node: it keeps what a guest said and what happened, so nobody has to ask twice. https://ivandemurard.com/anima
- **Peritia** (Design). The trade agent: a house's know-how, held by the house rather than by whoever is on shift. Named in the contract, no code. No page of its own.
- **Orchestrator** (Design, a proto-stub exists). The supervisory agent: a stateless router with no memory of its own. It routes between the others and holds the decision.

## 1. Why several agents and not one

The tempting shape is one large model that predicts, decides and acts. It collapses in practice,
because forecasting and acting have different failure modes, different feedback loops and different
audit requirements. A wrong forecast is absorbed by a buffer. A wrong action reaches a guest, a
shift roster, or an aircraft. Each capability became a node with a strict boundary, and the
boundaries are enforced by the protocol rather than by discipline.

## 2. One scene, four signals

Illustration, not a capability: nothing in this system performs check-in today.

Check-in looks like a process, and optimising it as one gives you the metric a process offers: time
to key. A fast, cold arrival is an excellent process and a bad welcome. Four signals meet in one
arrival, and each belongs to a different agent:

- Tacet: what is happening outside, since a transit strike lands every arrival in the same twenty minutes.
- Aetherix: how full the house is tonight, and what that does to the service that follows.
- Anima: whether this guest has stayed before and what they asked for last time. For a first stay: nothing to recall, and it says so.
- Peritia: who is on the desk, how loaded they are, how far into the shift.

This is why guest experience is not an agent of its own. An agent that owned it would have to own
all four domains, and an agent that owns everything is not a bounded context.

Time to key can be predicted. Whether someone felt welcomed cannot. That gap is a property of the
problem, not of the data, and it holds harder at check-out, which carries the payment and weighs
most in memory.

## 3. The five agents

| Agent | Status | Owns | Does not own |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Aetherix | Built, 0 real users, forecast in shadow mode, pilot partner in recruitment | F&B execution: covers forecast, staffing grid, waste risk, per-property memory | Orchestration, pricing, guest-facing anything |
| Tacet | Built, maintenance mode since July 2026 | External signal: weather, street, events, ray-traced acoustic impact, yield rules | Deciding anything. It publishes rules for approval |
| Anima | Synthetic PoC, production DPIA-gated | Guest memory: what a guest said and what happened, four layers, each claim with source, confidence and age | Acting on it, or returning a whole person: every query declares one layer |
| Peritia | Design | House knowledge: what the people who work in a property know and never wrote down | Everything. It is a named slot in the contract, and no code |
| Orchestrator | Design, stateless router, no memory | Supervisory routing and business rules across agents | Domain logic and memory. It routes, it does not compute and it stores nothing |

Fig. 3.1, on the web page, wires the four domain agents to the orchestrator at the centre: a solid spoke for what is built, a dashed spoke for what is designed and not written. The orchestrator holds no memory of its own; state stays with the agent that owns it, and no agent talks to another. Selecting a mark shows what that agent owns and what it does not own, with the same wording as the table above.

Aetherix executes. It does not orchestrate.


## 4. Five rules that hold it together

1. **One bounded context per node.** A node that owns two domains arbitrates between them privately,
   and the arbitration stops being reviewable.
2. **MCP is the only doorway.** Nodes do not import each other. Every exchange is a tool call, so
   every exchange is loggable, auditable and priceable, and a node can be replaced without its
   neighbours knowing. Until the orchestrator is built (Design), Tacet's output reaches Aetherix
   directly: the one documented exception, non-personal, read-only, logged. Target: every exchange
   goes through the orchestrator.
3. **Tenancy is resolved server-side, never passed as an argument.** The property identifier is
   established by the server at every layer. What a model cannot name, it cannot cross.
4. **Memory is local first, federated second, and never raw.** Each property learns from its own
   history; cross-property learning moves only as anonymised aggregates. Local memory is as
   described. Federation: Research, no substrate yet.
5. **A fifth agent is an addition, not a redesign.** The contract that governs exchanges between
   agents was designed to admit staff knowledge: what the people who work in a property know, which
   nothing captures today. That agent is named Peritia, the trade agent: a house's know-how, held by
   the house rather than by whoever is on shift. Not started, and no code.

## 5. What each node is allowed to learn

| Node | Feedback available | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetherix | Manager replies, plus forecast compared against the actual figure | Can measure itself and gate on the result |
| Tacet | Rejections of its alerts, per coordinate | Learns local shielding without ground truth on the outcome |
| Anima | Guest signals, sparse and regulated | Learns slowly by design, and must forget on request |
| Orchestrator | None of its own | Judged only by whether the nodes it routed to were right |

A node with an outcome loop can be allowed to adjust itself. A node without one has to be gated
before it ships, because nothing downstream will catch it. See the field note
https://ivandemurard.com/journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops

## 6. Where the sector's twins stop

Digital twins are mature elsewhere: market scenarios in banking, data centres at Google, warehouses
at Amazon, decades of aerospace and automotive use. In hospitality they model the building:
predictive maintenance, refurbishment simulation, energy optimisation. Searching for one that
simulates the impact of an operational decision before it is taken, a staffing change, an F&B order,
a service adjustment, returns nothing. The sector models its assets and not its arbitrations. This
architecture is not marketed as a twin and does not simulate scenarios today. Anima included: a
guest memory, not a twin.

## 7. Verification and pointers

The statuses above are the claim. Here is where to check them.

Public meta-repository: https://github.com/IvandeMurard/Hospitality-Multi-agent-Architecture

The field note "Evaluating LLM agents: how would you know it had stopped working?" explains how a
system earns the right to ship. This page explains what the systems are.
https://ivandemurard.com/journal/harnesses-graders-closed-loops

Contact: ivandemurard@gmail.com, https://cal.com/ivandemurard/discussion-and-introduction

## Query this architecture from your agent

The five agents talk over MCP. So does this site: a public, read-only MCP server exposes the case studies, the field notes and the bio as tools.

claude mcp add ivandemurard --transport http https://lzzlepzecynpztipkdcu.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp
